transcript: You have some. The fish was as long as Jab's thumb, smoked black by a lifetime of hanging near a fire, with one fin broken off before Tonk was born. And that was knowing. That was the rail's ground. The rail rode out over nothing on the corners, and Jab took every one of them slowly, with his weight into the hill, feeling for where his own width had gone. Twice he had to stop and back up and take a corner at a different angle, because the rail had found a root or a rock and he could not see it and could only feel the frame try to turn him. At the fourth rest he set the frame's foot on a boulder and leaned forward into the belt with his hands on his knees and breathed until the gray went out of the edges of things. Four. Tonk said behind his ear. Four. It's not so many. It's alright. Jab. And he put it back, and after a moment it came again, faint, unmistakable, and entirely useless, since he had no idea what it was or what to do with it.
